thread:
Mira: quick check — I ran a tiny speculative decode pass on the Llama3-lite quant (4-bit) we just onboarded. curious about perf vs quality tradeoffs.
Alex: nice, what config?
Mira: baseline greedy on quant model, then speculative with draft_size=2, topk=5 fallback, kv-cache enabled. batch=8.
Mira: command: ```python run_infer.py --model llama3-lite-q4 --mode speculative --draft_size 2 --topk 5 --batch 8 --kv_cache```
Sam: results? numbers please :)
Mira: throughput up ~1.9x tokens/sec vs greedy on same quant. p50 latency increased ~10ms but p95 dropped for batched requests.
Jin: interesting — did you compare quality on our eval set?
Mira: yes, ran the onboarding eval set (500 prompts) and MMLU-style tasks subset (math+commonsense).
Mira: quality: exact-match accuracy dropped 1.7% on short-answer subset, BLEU-ish metric for generation tasks dropped 0.8.
Alex: that's small but nontrivial. any patterns on where it regressed?
Mira: common failure modes: hallucinations on long-context reasoning and truncated completions when draft diverged then fallback corrected halfway.
Sam: was fallback frequency high?
Mira: fallback triggered ~12% of tokens (i.e., when draft topk didn't cover gold continuation). Most of those recovered correctness but some produced incoherent tails.
Jin: could be due to quant noise — 4-bit QAT/PTQ? which quant method?
Mira: PTQ (GPTQ-style) with per-channel scales. We also tried a quick QAT run but only for 1 epoch on subset; quality improved 0.6% but cost to train was nontrivial.
Alex: what's the latency win if we raise draft_size to 3?
Mira: draft_size=3 -> throughput 2.3x but fallback jumps to ~19%, and accuracy drop grows to ~3.2% on short-answer. diminishing returns and more quality risk.
Sam: can we tune topk or temperature for fewer fallbacks?
Mira: topk=8 reduced fallbacks to 9% but throughput drops to 1.6x. temp=0.7 slightly reduces bad tails but introduces randomness on deterministic tasks.
Jin: suggestion: targeted speculative only on prefix-heavy workloads (chat-like) and disable for math/structured outputs. Can we auto-route based on prompt classifier?
Mira: I prototyped a simple heuristic: if prompt contains code/math keywords -> force greedy. On eval split that reduced regressions by ~40% while preserving 70% of speedups across chat prompts.
Alex: solid. How about combining with cache priming? e.g., if prefix seen before, use larger draft_size; unseen prefixes use smaller.
Mira: implemented a cheap LRU prefix store. For repeated prefixes speedups go to 2.6x and fallbacks under 8%.
Sam: what's our recommended default for hosted API then?
Mira: proposal: enable speculative default for non-structured prompts with draft_size=2, topk=6; add prompt classifier for structured tasks -> force greedy. Add opt-in per-route in console.
Jin: need an eval gating: if rollout causes >1% absolute drop on any core QA benchmark, auto-disable.
Alex: yes add a rollout stage: 5% traffic canary -> monitor MMLU_short, reasoning precision, and token-level hallucination metric.
Mira: I'll draft the rollout plan and a short eval harness patch.
EvalBot: automated eval completed: canary sim (5% traffic) projected net cost reduction 21%, projected accuracy delta -1.1% on MMLU_short.
Sam: thanks — looks like we should proceed with caution. Mira if you can post the draft rollout + eval script I'll vet and we can spin up a canary tomorrow.
Mira: will do, uploading patch and eval logs in a minute. :thumbsup:
Alex: ping me when uploaded, I want to add a config option in the router for per-customer policy.
Jin: and I'll start a short QAT job to see if we can recover the 1.1% hit without losing latency.
Mira: noted — uploading now. Logs: ```s3://redwood-onboard/llama3-lite/spec_scan/1923456789/logs.tar.gz```
Mira: tl;dr: speculative gives meaningful cost/throughput win on chatty workloads, small quality regressions on reasoning tasks — mitigations look promising.
